You need a YouTube API key the moment your app has to read anything from YouTube: a video's length, its view count, a channel's latest uploads. Getting one takes about five minutes. Using it well takes a little longer, because YouTube changed how its quota works in June 2026, and plenty of guides still describe the old rules.

Industry observers note that in this guide we'll get a key, lock it down and test it. Then we'll use it from Node.js for three real jobs: adding up the length of a playlist, listing a channel's videos without spending a search, and estimating what a video earned. Along the way we'll cover what the YouTube API costs (nothing), how the 2026 quota works, and the errors you're most likely to hit.

According to recent reports, A YouTube API key identifies your project to the YouTube Data API v3. With just a key, you can read public data:.

Sources indicate that A key isn't enough for anything that touches someone's account. Uploading videos, editing playlists or reading private data needs OAuth 2.0, where the user signs in and grants your app access.

According to recent reports, you'll need a Google account. The YouTube Data API is free, so there's nothing to pay for.

It has been revealed that the restrictions matter more than they look. A key is just a string in a URL, and anyone who copies an unrestricted one can spend your daily quota for you. With an API restriction, the key is useless for other Google APIs. With an application restriction, it only works from your server or your site. Changes to restrictions can take up to five minutes to apply, so don't panic if a request fails straight after you save.

In a recent development, before writing any code, check the key with a single request. This one asks for the first video ever uploaded to YouTube, and uses the fields parameter to trim the response down to four values:.

If the key works, you'll get this back:.

That request cost 1 unit of your daily quota, which brings us to the question everyone asks.

Yes. There's no charge per request and no paid plan. Instead you get a daily quota, and since June 1, 2026 it's split into separate buckets:.

According to recent reports, google's quota calculator lists the cost of every method. Quotas reset at midnight Pacific Time. Every request costs at least 1 unit, including requests that fail, so a retry loop around a broken call can use up a day's quota on its own.

If you've read older guides, search is the massive change. A search used to cost 100 units out of the same 10,000, so 100 searches emptied your whole day. Uploads were worse still, at about 1,600 units each until December 2025. Now both have their own buckets, and the 10,000 units are left for everything else.

To give you a feel for what 10,000 units buys, here's what each example in this guide costs:.

It has been revealed that you can't pay for more. To go above the defaults, fill in the YouTube API Services Audit and Quota Extension Form, which is linked from Google's page on quota and compliance audits. YouTube first audits your project to check it follows the YouTube API Services Terms of Service, then someone from the API team gets back to you. Google doesn't give a timeline, so apply well before you need the extra quota.

Most projects never need to. The rest of this guide is about getting a lot done with very few units.

Industry observers note that the examples need Node.js 20.6 or later, for the built-in fetch and the --env-file flag. There are no packages to install. Make a folder with a .env file in it:.

Sources indicate that every example imports one small helper. It builds the URL, adds your key and turns API errors into readable messages:.

Run any example with node --env-file=.env followed by the file name.

YouTube doesn't tell you how long a playlist is. To work it out, you need two methods:.

In a recent development, durations come back in ISO 8601 format. PT15M33S is 15 minutes 33 seconds, PT1H2M3S adds an hour, and a stream longer than a day looks like P1DT2H3M4S. The toSeconds() function below handles all three.

Here it is on freeCodeCamp's Full Courses in One Video playlist:.

Industry observers note that that's 184 hours of courses for 4 units of quota. Private and deleted videos still show up in a playlist's items, but videos.list doesn't return them, which is why the script prints "52 of 52 videos available". On a playlist with removed videos, the two numbers will differ.

This is the core of the free YouTube playlist length calculator I built on createthat.ai. The live version adds a target time box that works out the speed you need to finish by a deadline, and it accepts channel, video and Shorts links as well as playlists.

Recent findings suggest that the obvious way to find a channel's videos is to search for them. Don't: search is now capped at 100 calls a day, and it isn't built to list everything a channel has posted. Every channel has an uploads playlist instead, and you can reach it in two cheap calls:.

Recent findings suggest that two units, and none of your 100 daily searches. To get every upload rather than the newest five, page through the playlist with the same pageToken loop as Example 1.

videos.list with part=statistics returns a video's view, like and comment counts. Dislike counts have been private since December 2021 and favoriteCount is always 0, so don't build anything on those. The script also copes with a missing like or comment count, which you'll see on some videos.

This time the fields parameter trims the response to the values we use. That makes the response smaller, but it doesn't change the cost: the call is 1 unit either way.

Here it is on freeCodeCamp's Learn Python full course, one of the most-watched videos in that playlist:.

Treat the last line as a rough range, not an answer. The Data API doesn't share anyone's revenue, so any estimate is views multiplied by an RPM: what a creator keeps per 1,000 views. RPM moves a lot with the topic and where the viewers live, and the estimate assumes the video indicates ads, which not every channel does.

Sources indicate that and sometimes you don't need an API at all. When I built a font tester, I needed a list of Google Fonts. The Google Fonts Developer API would have meant a key and a call on every visit, for a list that barely changes. Instead I generated a file of the 500 most popular fonts once, from Google's public font metadata, and the page loads it like any other file. No key, no quota and nothing to fail.

When a call fails, the response's error.message and error.details[0].reason tell you why. These are the ones you'll see most:.

Yes. Creating a key and calling the YouTube Data API costs nothing. You're limited by the daily quota instead, and there's no paid tier: more quota comes through an audit.

In a recent development, in the Google Cloud console, select your project and go to APIs & Services > Credentials. Your keys are listed under API keys, with a Show key option next to each one.

It has been revealed that it works, but anyone can read the key from your page. If you do it, restrict the key to your website and to the YouTube Data API v3. A small server route that calls the API for you is safer, and it gives you somewhere to cache results.

By default, 100 searches, 100 uploads and 10,000 units for everything else. Most reads cost 1 unit and videos.list takes 50 IDs per call, so that's enough for the details of up to 500,000 videos a day.

Sources indicate that getting a YouTube API key is the easy part: one project, one API to enable, one key and two restrictions. The 2026 quota is generous if you work with it:.

On November 20, a horse named I Show Speed won the Jefferies Australia Class 2 Handicap at Bong Bong racecourse in Australia.

The four-year-old gelding, trained by Todd Smart and ridden by jockey Leandro Ribeiro, finished 1.3 lengths ahead of second-place Mystic Air in the 1,000-metre race.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A family-owned restaurant called Oscar’s has been left stunned after discovering that their business seemingly appears in GTA 6.

GTA 6 has finally arrived, allowing players to explore Rockstar Games’ fictional state of Leonida, which takes heavy inspiration from Florida and features countless locations modelled on real-life landmarks.

Since its November 19 release, players have been discovering familiar locations throughout the game, but one family was particularly surprised to find their own restaurant recreated in Rockstar’s open world.

On November 21, X user @sirenaslloran shared her emotional reaction after discovering that her family’s restaurant, Oscar’s, had seemingly been recreated in GTA 6.

According to recent reports, “Guys my family’s restaurant made it onto GTA 6. I’m crying so bad,” she wrote. “My parents are immigrants who came here with a dream and now we’ve been voted by the city as the number one breakfast spot and now this.”.

She explained that her parents had immigrated to the United States hoping to build a successful business and that their restaurant had since been voted the city’s number-one breakfast spot.

In a recent development, oscar’s has two locations and is family owned & operated ! Thank you so much for the support & kind messages. I’m reading them all to my family & my abuela notes “gracias y que Dios los bendiga siempre”. 🩷 https://t.co/9EgmdobDsj pic.twitter.com/8fIGviTcnU.

In a follow-up post, she revealed that Oscar’s is a family-owned and operated business with two locations. She also explained that she had been reading the messages aloud to her family, sharing a particularly touching response from her grandmother.

“Gracias y que Dios los bendiga siempre,” her grandmother noted, which translates to “Thank you, and may God always bless you.”.

Industry News: GTA 6 boss explains why classic mini-games from previous games are missing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 boss Rob Nelson has explained why players aren’t able to play classic minigames like darts and bowling, despite there being some nods to them in-game.
  • In a recent development, after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to sink their teeth into GTA 6 and all that Leonida has to offer.
  • It has been revealed that however, if you look around The Rusty Anchor and other bars around the state of Leonida, you will notice that darts is missing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 boss Rob Nelson has explained why players aren’t able to play classic minigames like darts and bowling, despite there being some nods to them in-game.

In a recent development, after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to sink their teeth into GTA 6 and all that Leonida has to offer. Early on in the story, you’re introduced to one of the classic GTA mini-games: pool.

It has been revealed that however, if you look around The Rusty Anchor and other bars around the state of Leonida, you will notice that darts is missing. Plus, there is the Kingpin bowling alley in Port Gellhorn, but you can’t relive your days as Niko and Roman, tossing strikes down the lanes.

Well, Rockstar’s Rob Nelson told VGC that a “lot of work” is needed to get the minigames and activities right, but they “didn’t have the resources” to bring Darts and Bowling back.

“The darts one is a contentious one,” Nelson mentioned. “Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to.”.

Nelson noted that gym activities, like Weightlifting, extend beyond just button mashing. “It mimics what weightlifting is,” he added.

It has been revealed that “A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn’t get to. It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough.”.

The Rockstar North co-studio head added that pool has “proper physics” and is a “game in its own right.”.

Despite missing darts and bowling, Rockstar’s long-awaited release has paid off in spades. It has become the joint best-reviewed game of all time, matching Ocarina of Time.

If only there were a cheat code that could help you turn Jason into Luke Littler on a dartboard. That would have been a nice touch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

It has been revealed that A designer who once spent an afternoon searching stock libraries can now describe the picture they want and have four versions in under a minute. AI image generators have moved from curiosity to everyday tool for blog headers, product mockups, ad concepts, game art and slide decks. The quality gap between tools has narrowed, but the differences that remain matter a lot: how well each follows a detailed prompt, whether it can render readable text, how it handles edits, and what you are allowed to do with the result.

Recent findings suggest that this guide compares six of the best-known options, what each does well and where each falls short. Models, prepares and limits change often, so check each vendor's own pages before you commit to a workflow.

OpenArt’s AI image generator puts several image models behind one interface. Its generator page lists models including GPT Image 2.5, Grok Imagine, Qwen Image 3, Nano Banana 2 and Seedream 5.0 Pro, and lets you create images from text prompts or reference photos. It also lists tools for camera angle control, upscaling, collages and a Character Builder for keeping characters consistent across scenes, with 4K export.

Best for: Creators who want to compare several models on the same prompt without juggling separate subscriptions and accounts.

Recent findings suggest that limitations: The page offers a free start but does not state credit amounts or plan details, and it does not address commercial use, so check the pricing and licensing pages before using results for client work. Output quality depends on which model you pick.

It has been revealed that openAI's image generation in ChatGPT works inside the chat interface, which makes iteration natural: generate an image, then ask for changes in plain language. OpenAI highlights accurate text rendering, the ability to follow prompts with many distinct objects, and consistent characters across multi-turn edits. You can also upload reference images and have the model transform them. It handles both photorealistic and stylized looks.

Best for: Marketers and writers who want to describe, refine and re-describe an image without learning a latest tool.

According to recent reports, limitations: OpenAI notes that tall images such as posters can be cropped too tightly, and that dense small text, multilingual text and precise graphs can still go wrong. Images can take up to a minute to render. All generated images carry C2PA metadata identifying their source.

Recent findings suggest that gemini's image generation runs on Google's Nano Banana models. Google highlights character consistency, text rendering in many languages, combining several photos, precise editing and 2K resolution. A free tier covers image generation and editing, while the most advanced model requires a Google AI blueprint. You start from the "Create images" option in the Gemini app, then prompt or upload a picture to edit.

Best for: People who need to keep the same subject across several images, or who want to edit existing photos quickly.

Recent findings suggest that limitations: Usage limits apply, and the strongest model is behind a paid strategy. Images include an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible AI label, which is good for transparency but may not suit every use.

According to recent reports, midjourney is an independent research lab known for images with a strong, painterly look. Its official site points owners to a sign-up flow and to a Discord community and help center for support. Many creators choose it for concept art, mood boards and illustration where style matters more than literal accuracy.

Best for: Artists, art directors and game designers who want rich, stylized results and enjoy exploring variations.

According to recent reports, limitations: I could not confirm current pricing, trial terms or feature details from Midjourney's public pages, so check them yourself before subscribing. The workflow can feel less like a normal app than the others on this list, and it is not the easiest route for precise, text-heavy graphics.

In a recent development, adobe Firefly is built for professionals who already work in Creative Cloud. Adobe states that its Firefly models are commercially safe, trained on licensed Adobe Stock and public domain content, and outputs carry Content Credentials that show AI involvement. It offers text-to-image, image-to-image, sketch-to-image and style transfer, plus editing tools such as background removal, object removal, upscaling and generative expand. It connects with Photoshop, Illustrator, Lightroom and Adobe Express, and also lets you use partner models from other companies.

Best for: Designers and brand teams who need clear licensing and want AI inside the apps they already use.

Limitations: Plans work on a credit system, so heavy use adds up. Adobe lists a free tier with limited daily generations and paid plans starting at about $9.99 a month, but confirm current terms on its site.

Ideogram built its reputation on a problem that trips up many generators: readable text. Its current models are presented as producing clean typography in different layouts, with attention to prompt fidelity and reliable editing. It also offers an API with access to a catalog of models, and has released open weights for one earlier model for local use and customization under its license.

Best for: Posters, social graphics, logo concepts and anything where words are part of the image.

According to recent reports, limitations: The pages I checked did not describe a free blueprint, so look at current looks before relying on it. Like every generator, it still needs a human to proofread the text it produces.

Industry observers note that start with the job. If you want to compare several models side by side, try OpenArt. If you want to talk your way to a finished image, try ChatGPT or Gemini. If you need images that will sit inside a branded design workflow, Firefly is the safer fit. If you are chasing a distinctive look, Midjourney deserves a trial. If text must be perfect, test Ideogram.

Industry observers note that run the same prompt in two or three tools before paying. Differences in composition, hands, faces and text show up quickly, and they matter more than any feature list.

According to recent reports, reviews only go so far, because your own use case is what counts. Pick one realistic job, for example a 16:9 header image for a blog post about web performance, and run the same prompt through two or three tools. Write the prompt once and paste it unchanged, so the comparison is fair:.

Then score each result on five questions: Did it follow every instruction? Are there odd details in hands, edges or objects? Is any text spelled correctly? Does it still look good when cropped to a square? Could you license it for your project? Ten minutes of this teaches more than any feature list, and it shows how much editing each tool needs before you can publish.

Most readers of this guide will put these images on web pages, where a few habits matter more than the generator you choose.

It has been revealed that there is no single best AI image generator. The right pick depends on whether you value conversation, style, licensing, control or typography. Test two or three on a real project, compare the output, and keep a human in charge of the final choice. Whatever you generate, review it for errors and label AI-made images clearly where your audience would expect it.

Are AI-generated images free to use commercially? It depends on the provider and your plan. Read the licensing terms for the tool you use, and consider vendors that publish how their models were trained if you work for clients.

Recent findings suggest that which AI image generator is best for text in images? Ideogram and ChatGPT both highlight text rendering, and Gemini lists it as a feature. Test each with your own wording and proofread the result.

Do AI images have watermarks? Some do. OpenAI adds C2PA metadata, Google adds an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible label, and Adobe attaches Content Credentials.

Can I use more than one image model without separate accounts? Yes. Platforms such as OpenArt put several models in one interface, which makes side-by-side testing easier. Check the licensing terms for each model you use.

Should I add alt text to AI-generated images? Yes, when the image carries meaning. Describe what it indicates or why it is there. Purely decorative images can use an empty alt attribute, following the W3C guidance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The actor behind an NPC in GTA 6 is sending players on a manhunt to find him, as he has no idea who his character actually is.

GTA 6 had been in development for a long time before it arrived on November 19. This means that many actors who appear in the game may have had to wait years to see their work fully realized in Vice City.

That’s exactly what happened to Guy A. Fortt, who is named in the GTA 6 credits. In fact, it’s been so long since he actually gave Rockstar his performance, he no longer remembers who he’s even playing.

“So, I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don’t know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in a video. “I auditioned about four or five years ago, they put the balls all over my body and face I was [gesturing], and then I forgot all about it.”.

According to recent reports, “Then I get a random email telling me that I’m in GTA 6. This is where I need your help.”.

.💪🏾 “From 9/11 First Responder to GTA 6 Motion Capture Actor! 🙏🏾”I have no clue pic.twitter.com/cqjxcS6E1N.

Industry observers note that he goes on to explain that he doesn’t play games and so doesn’t own a console, so he wants players to help him track down his character. Thankfully, he has a couple of clues to help the search.

It has been revealed that “All I know is I was behind the counter, I was standing there. I know the leads came in, they were talking to me [and] I had balls and stuff all over my face, and I was talking to them about something,” he continued.

Sources indicate that based on this description, it sounds like he is some kind of store clerk. Perhaps he’s the owner of one of the many stores that Jason and Lucia can rob across Leonida.

The following day, he posted an revision saying that three million players are at the moment on the hunt for his character, admitting he had “no clue” what Grand Theft Auto was or how big it was.

However, despite the community’s best efforts, Fortt’s character remains a mystery at the time of writing.

Tech Report: Ex-Rockstar artist explains main difference between Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 open world

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A former Rockstar artist who worked on both GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 notes Leonida’s countryside has slightly less detail than the natural world of Rockstar’s Western.
  • Industry observers note that david O’Reilly made the comparison while exploring GTA 6’s Mount Kalaga region, an area he worked on before leaving Rockstar in 2023.
  • O’Reilly believes Red Dead 2 gave its landscapes more attention because they made up so much of the game’s world, while GTA 6 has a dense modern city to bring to life alongside its countryside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A former Rockstar artist who worked on both GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 notes Leonida’s countryside has slightly less detail than the natural world of Rockstar’s Western.

Industry observers note that david O’Reilly made the comparison while exploring GTA 6’s Mount Kalaga region, an area he worked on before leaving Rockstar in 2023. He was impressed by what he found, describing the game’s presentation as “almost flawless,” but noticed a difference in where the two games put their detail.

O’Reilly believes Red Dead 2 gave its landscapes more attention because they made up so much of the game’s world, while GTA 6 has a dense modern city to bring to life alongside its countryside.

“I’m seeing a slight paring back in the natural world in GTA 6 from RDR2, but obviously a much greater emphasis and much more kind of detail in the urban environments,” O’Reilly remarked in a video sharing his first impressions.

He also found GTA 6’s cities more interactive and immersive, saying the difference reflected the kind of world each game was built to portray.

“GTA 6 is more a systems-driven modern urban world with countryside, natural landscapes, whereas RDR2 was almost purely natural landscapes,” he explained. This was especially noticeable in the game’s rivers, which he worked on as a water artist for Red Dead 2.

Industry observers note that “Rivers were a bigger emphasis on RDR2. They were a massive part of the world, and in this game they’re a lesser part of the world,” he remarked. After examining the water around Mount Kalaga, O’Reilly added that, “on balance,” he prefers Red Dead 2’s rivers and thinks GTA 6’s water is generally “a little bit too slow.”.

He praised the way GTA 6’s water continues to react to players and objects even when they stop moving, though, calling it “a significant plus point.” O’Reilly was also impressed by the riverbanks themselves, saying the rocks on either side were “blowing my mind.”.

In a recent development, despite giving Red Dead 2 the edge when it comes to natural landscapes, O’Reilly expects to spend plenty more time travelling around Leonida. After a canoe trip through Mount Kalaga, he noted GTA 6 would probably replace Red Dead 2 as his “go-to chill game” when he wants to relax.

AI-friendly pages are plain-text (usually markdown) versions of webpages that are meant for AI, rather than people. Websites typically determine that AI is requesting a page via the user agent, Accept header, or a specific .md URL.

We ran this test at acme.bot on November 4, 2026, across 53 live pages on 43 host names. Because we targeted sites likely to do this, the sample leans towards developer tools.

While testing the HubSpot, Gymshark, Semrush and Profound web pages, we didn't find any markdown on the pages.

While it's a common practice in developer documentation, there's not much research or evidence that it helps AI visibility.

In a recent development, dries Buytaert checked a month of Cloudflare logs and found no AI crawler using content negotiation. The crawlers reached his markdown only through dedicated URLs, by following an auto-discovery link. So a site that relies on Accept alone is serving coding agents - and, possibly, no crawlers at all.

Sources indicate that even when the request asks for HTML, Stripe's docs still send markdown to all six AI user agents we tested. They send HTML to Bingbot, Googlebot, and browsers. The Checkout page drops from 846 KB to 5.5 KB. Its markdown has links to other .md pages, keeping an agent in the text pages. The response to markdown comes with the header X-Robots-Tag: none to ensure it is kept out of search indexes. Sentry's docs route the same way.

Vercel pages (including the blog and pricing page) that we tried all returned markdown on request. Docs pages also go to AI user agents, unless the request prefers HTML. Pricing and blog pages do not. The Next.js docs exhibit a similar behavior.

Neon delivers markdown on docs and pricing to non-browser clients that do not prefer HTML, including plain curl.

Sources indicate that neon's page isn't just a conversion. The markdown copy of its introduction is about 3,070 words, against roughly 620 in the visible HTML, and it speaks directly to the agent: "The user needs a Neon account." This sentence, however, is not in the HTML. Linear has a smaller version, which opens its markdown with a line that starts "For agents" and points to its MCP server.

Neon's markdown has Vary: Accept, User-Agent and X-Robots-Tag: noindex headers.

Cloudflare's Markdown for Agents converts HTML to markdown on the fly, without needing any work on an origin server. It's available on the Pro strategy and above and handles up to 6 MiB of HTML. Cloudflare reports one post falling from 16,180 tokens to 3,150.

1. Fix the HTML first. Vercel's guide says it plainly: "Make the HTML work before adding a Markdown mirror." Render the content on the server, because many AI crawlers don't run JS.

2. Generate markdown from the same source as the HTML. That keeps the two versions in step when the page changes.

3. Answer Accept: text/markdown. Return Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8 at the same URL, with a fallback to HTML when there's no markdown.

It has been revealed that 4. Publish .md URLs and link to them. Each page should have a added to it. In Buytaert's logs, this is the route the crawlers took.

It has been revealed that 5. Add user agent detection only if you need it. Identify the agents you want to serve, and omit search engines. Should the list include training crawlers? Stripe's does and Mintlify's doesn't. Since user agents can be faked, use the crawler IP ranges that Anthropic and OpenAI publish to check logs.

Sources indicate that 6. Set the cache key. Send Vary: Accept, and also User-Agent if it determines the response. Otherwise, a shared cache can give a person the markdown.

7. Keep the markdown out of search results. Use either a Link header to canonicalize the page to the HTML or add an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header.

It has been revealed that 8. Log the Accept header. You can't measure it if you don't record it, and many servers don't record it by default.

The evidence of benefit is thin, and it measures crawling, not citations.

Sources indicate that google's John Mueller called converting pages "such a stupid idea". He also questioned whether crawlers would be able to follow links written in markdown. Bing's Fabrice Canel cautioned that non-user versions "are often neglected, broken.".

In a recent development, google's spam policies define cloaking as a website showing different content to Googlebot than it would to customers. In our controlled test, all sites kept Googlebot on HTML. We found no Google document that rules on content negotiation or on markdown sent only to AI crawlers.

According to recent reports, if your site is developer documentation, making you site agent friendly is cheap, and your readers' coding agents already ask for it. So, answer Accept: text/markdown requests and publish linked .md URLs. Keep both out of the index.

For a marketing site, the case is not that strong. No study yet highlights more AI citations, and maintaining two copies of every page over time will be an overhead.

If citations are the goal, freshness looks like a stronger lever than format. In our study of 356 cited pages for getting cited by ChatGPT, typical article was two years old - but seven in ten had been edited in the last year.

Sources indicate that “I just thought, ‘oh my God, he’s done it again,’” Burroughs told the BBC. Before moving to Braintree, Zeus had made trips from his former home in Stansted Mountfitchet to London Stansted Airport.

But the percentage does not tell a developer what will happen when the integration reaches production. Extra JavaScript, unstable ad slots, opaque reporting, and difficult rollbacks can change the value of an apparently attractive deal.

In a recent development, for teams maintaining an advertising-funded website, choosing a Multiple Customer Management (MCM) partner is partly an engineering decision. The integration affects page templates, consent handling, third-party requests, account access, and monitoring. Those changes deserve the same scrutiny as a newly introduced analytics SDK or payment integration.

It has been revealed that this guide explains how to compare revenue shares on a consistent basis, review integration requirements, and test an ad setup without sacrificing usability. The goal is a repeatable evaluation process, rather than a universal winner.

Sources indicate that google Ad Manager’s MCM system lets a parent publisher manage a child publisher’s account or delegated inventory. The commercial agreement defines the partner’s services and compensation. Before comparing offers, ask which revenue streams the quoted percentage covers and whether the reporting figure is before or after that fee.

Use three separate lines in your evaluation spreadsheet:.

Revenue base: record the amount to which the partner’s percentage applies. Advertiser spending, exchange-reported revenue, and publisher earnings are different figures. Do not treat them as interchangeable.

It has been revealed that partner compensation: identify the percentage, fixed charges, and any optional services. Ask whether the same terms apply to every demand source and ad format.

Recent findings suggest that adjustments: distinguish estimated revenue from finalized earnings, including invalid-traffic deductions and other corrections. Document when adjustments appear and which party bears them.

A common mistake is applying the partner fee twice because a dashboard already displays net revenue. Label each exported metric before using it in a comparison.

It has been revealed that the two delegation models have different implications for access, reporting, and payments. Google’s documentation is the starting point for checking the proposed setup.

Manage Account gives the parent edit access within the child’s account while the child retains access and permissions. Payment facilitation can allocate eligible earnings from the child’s primary Ad Exchange account, but it does not automatically cover every third-party revenue stream. Confirm the invitation’s payment percentage and the separate commercial agreement.

Sources indicate that manage Inventory lets the parent manage delegated inventory in its own account, without access to the child account. Reporting for that inventory sits in the parent account. Google pays the parent for the relevant inventory, and the parent pays the child according to their agreement. Ask how you will obtain reports and reconcile payments.

Before implementation, document who can change tags, ad units, consent settings, and demand configuration. Agree on access for debugging and exporting historical data. A developer should be able to trace a production request to its configuration owner.

Confirm onboarding and exit costs.

Recent findings suggest that use this table as a request-for-information checklist. It does not rank providers or assert that any named service supports a particular implementation. Obtain current terms and technical documentation for the product you are considering.

In a recent development, apply the same standards to every proposal. The following examples show what a developer should ask during evaluation; each question is relevant across providers.

It has been revealed that monetizeMore offers publisher monetization products, including PubGuru and Traffic Cop. When evaluating its proposal, connect the commercial discussion to concrete integration questions: which scripts will load, who owns the configuration, and how will reported earnings be reconciled?

Record device, geography, page type, and consent state so differences in traffic mix do not masquerade as a revenue improvement.

Keep a dated deployment log connecting each configuration version with the reporting period.

Decision criterion: a measured comparison should separate implementation changes from changes in audience or demand.

Check spacing, responsive behavior, keyboard navigation, and whether sticky placements obscure content or controls.

Reserve space for expected ad dimensions and test what happens when no ad is returned.

Compare layout stability before and after the change.

List required changes to scripts, plugins, caching, DNS, or delivery infrastructure, if any. Do not assume that every deployment uses the same method.

Test interactions with your consent manager, content security policy, caching rules, and existing analytics.

Document how to remove the integration and restore the prior configuration.

Decision criterion: the operational cost should be visible before the first production rollout.

Ask who creates ad slots, updates templates, and validates responsive sizes.

Request a support escalation process with the diagnostic information required for an incident: URL, timestamp, device, consent state, and affected slot.

Recent findings suggest that with the same traffic volume, revenue definition, and deduction rate, the break-even increase in pre-partner revenue is: (current publisher share ÷ newly introduced publisher share) − 1. Express shares consistently as fractions or percentages. The table below highlights the required lift; it is not a forecast these thresholds only describe the arithmetic. Different ad density, audience mix, deduction rates, or reporting bases can invalidate the comparison. Normalize to the same denominator, such as revenue per thousand pageviews, and compare matched periods or properly assigned concurrent cohorts.

Assume two hypothetical setups each receive one million pageviews. Here, RPM means revenue per thousand pageviews before the partner fee. For this simplified example, deductions reduce that revenue before the publisher share is applied.

Partner A: $10 pre-partner RPM × 1,000 groups of pageviews × 0.90 after deductions × 0.90 publisher share = $8,100 net revenue.

Partner B: $12 pre-partner RPM × 1,000 groups of pageviews × 0.98 after deductions × 0.80 publisher share = $9,408 net revenue.

It has been revealed that the difference is $1,308 for the period despite Partner B’s lower share. These are illustrative inputs, not provider performance claims. Faster payment improves cash-flow timing; it does not, by itself, increase the revenue earned.

Verify that the page remains usable when the ad system fails. Automated tests should not click live advertisements or generate artificial monetized traffic.

Separate unit tests for configuration logic, integration tests for component boundaries, and browser tests for user-visible behavior. SitePoint’s explanation of unit, functional, and integration testing provides a useful foundation. Define rollback criteria before launch, keep the control configuration available, and review finalized revenue alongside performance data before expanding the deployment.

After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to jump into GTA 6 and, naturally, YouTubers and streamers want to share their experiences with everyone else.

As DarkViperAU showed, El Santo, otherwise known as Andrés Arango Flórez, has seemingly uploaded his videos to YouTube’s Content ID system, hence them being flagged.

“Yo my dude, you have put your GTA 6 playthrough in the Content ID system, and so are claiming GTA 6 gameplay livestreams. Please fix. Thanks,” he said.

Sources indicate that @FRANKELSANTO Yo my dude, you have put your GTA 6 playthrough in the Content ID system and so are claiming GTA 6 gameplay livestreams. Please fix. Thanks. pic.twitter.com/zoUkP8PiPz.

However, as per Polygon, Arango Flórez responded to the situation in the comments of one of his videos, passing the blame onto YouTube’s automated moderation system.

“Thank you for your patience, and again, sorry for the trouble.”.

More of the GTA 6 soundtrack may have leaked after artist comments.

YouTube’s content moderation system has routinely come under fire from creators, especially as appeal processes are also largely moderated by AI.

The platform has made changes over the years, but the same problems still come up.

“If it wants to use AI for moderation, it should only be able to flag channels internally and then put that up the ladder for a human being to look at,” YouTuber MoistCr1TiKaL said back in December 2025.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • YouTuber Charlotte Dobre would make YouTube commenters use their real names, if she had the power to implement a new rule on the platform.
  • There has been plenty of debate online over the years about whether or not people should be allowed to use personas and fake names to make comments on social media.
  • Like everywhere else, YouTube gives you the option to use your real name or a pseudonym, with plenty of people opting to reveal their true identities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

YouTuber Charlotte Dobre would make YouTube commenters use their real names, if she had the power to implement a new rule on the platform.

There has been plenty of debate online over the years about whether or not people should be allowed to use personas and fake names to make comments on social media.

Like everywhere else, YouTube gives you the option to use your real name or a pseudonym, with plenty of people opting to reveal their true identities. They don’t always leave comments, so it makes things easier on that front.

Speaking to Dexerto, YouTuber and podcast host Charlotte Dobre revealed that, if she had the power to add a fresh rule to YouTube, it would be to force people to expose their true identities when leaving comments.

“Some people aren’t going to like this; I think that you should have to use your real name to comment. Everybody’s very brave behind a keyboard, but I’m curious how mean people would be if their real name was attached to it,” Dobre, who has just introduced a pilot for her show Textuationships, remarked.

“I think people are emboldened by the fact that there are no repercussions for the stuff they say. Like, everything I say, there are repercussions for. I have to be so, so careful with what I say.

“I do think if there were consequences, ergo, like your name was attached to it, people would be a lot more careful.”.

The YouTuber noted that people have gotten angry at her in the comments over some of the advice she’s given out, especially when they believe she hasn’t given the ‘right’ advice.

YouTube will let other creators react live to your videos and keep the live ad revenue.

YouTubers will soon be able to strike down AI content impersonating them.

YouTube creators outraged as latest profanity guidelines wreak havoc.

There are still plenty of platforms that offer anonymity, especially when it comes to things like burner accounts.

Instagram has started monetizing parts of that too, testing paid subscriptions that let you view people’s stories without notifying the other person that you’ve viewed their content.

OpenArt’s AI video generator puts a range of video models behind one interface. Its page lists models such as Veo 3.1, Kling, Seedance, Wan, Hailuo and PixVerse, so you can run the same prompt on different engines and compare the results without managing separate accounts.

Credit counts are hard to compare, so convert them to clips. It has been revealed that proposal for waste. If you keep one usable clip out of every three attempts, your real cost per finished shot is about three times the sticker price. Test with short, low-resolution drafts, then render the winner at full quality.

Industry observers note that because every tool outputs short clips, the real work is assembly. A typical workflow is: write a shot list, generate two or three takes per shot, pick the best, normalize them to one format, join them and add captions and audio. FFmpeg handles the joining step from the command line:.

According to recent reports, matching resolution, frame rate and codec before joining avoids glitches at the cut points. For character consistency across shots, reuse the same reference image in every prompt and keep descriptions of the subject identical.

If the clip ends up on your own site, treat it like any other media. Provide a poster image, load metadata only until the visitor presses play, and include captions so deaf and hard-of-hearing people, and anyone watching without sound, can follow along. The W3C’s guidance on captions and subtitles explains what to include, and the MDN video element reference covers the attributes below.

Sources indicate that also write a text description or transcript near the video. Search engines and screen reader people cannot see the footage, so the surrounding text is what explains it.

In a recent development, short, structured prompts beat long, vague ones. Describe the elements in the order a director would:.

Change one element at a time between takes so you can tell which change improved the result.

According to recent reports, marketing demos show the best of a tool, so run your own test. Use the same prompt, duration and aspect ratio on each tool, generate a few takes and score them against a short checklist. Keep notes on how many credits each usable clip costs.

Recent findings suggest that run the same test again with an image-to-video input if your workflow starts from product photos or illustrations. That often exposes differences in consistency that text prompts hide.

Industry observers note that which AI video generator is best? There is no single winner. Veo is strong for audio, Runway for editing, Kling for motion, Luma for modifying footage and Firefly for licensing clarity. A multi-model tool such as OpenArt helps you compare them.

Can AI video generators make long videos? Not in one pass. Most models create short clips, so longer videos are built by extending or stitching clips together.

According to recent reports, is Sora still available? OpenAI revealed in March 2026 that it was shutting down the Sora app and API, so it is not a safe choice for upcoming projects.

Can I use AI videos commercially? Often, but it depends on the strategy and the underlying model. Read the current terms before publishing.

Sources indicate that how do I keep a character consistent across clips? Reuse the same reference image, keep the subject description identical in every prompt, and use character or reference tools where the platform offers them.

Should I add captions to AI-generated video? Yes. Captions help accessibility and viewers watching without sound, and they give search engines text to index.

Do I need a powerful computer? No. These services run in the cloud, so a browser and a stable connection are enough.

The best AI video generator depends on what you make. Start with a short test prompt, compare a few tools, and keep the one that gives you usable clips at a sensible credit cost. If you are not sure where to begin, a multi-model option such as OpenArt lets you try several engines before you settle on one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO after its Board of Directors unanimously voted to bring him back despite an ongoing investigation into national security concerns.
  • Recent findings suggest that huang had been temporarily replaced by Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress following reports that the executive had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
  • On November 23, Nvidia announced that Huang would return to his leadership positions effective immediately following a series of meetings with the board and consultations with senior US government officials.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO after its Board of Directors unanimously voted to bring him back despite an ongoing investigation into national security concerns.

Recent findings suggest that huang had been temporarily replaced by Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress following reports that the executive had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The reports prompted the organization’s board to establish an independent committee and retain outside legal counsel to investigate the matter.

On November 23, Nvidia announced that Huang would return to his leadership positions effective immediately following a series of meetings with the board and consultations with senior US government officials.

The controversy began in late October when The Newly introduced York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing manufacturer Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.

Megaspeed has also faced scrutiny over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia AI chips subject to US export restrictions. The Chinese government has denied the espionage allegations.

On November 8, Huang admitted in a message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia revealed its independent investigation that same day.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil.

Further reporting alleged that Huang had also engaged in an extramarital affair with Nvidia Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell. On November 12, the firm announced his resignation, ending his 33-year tenure as CEO.

However, less than two weeks later, Nvidia’s board reversed course, saying it was confident that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.

Sources indicate that “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Board Chair Harvey C. Jones stated.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy controversy.

Nvidia launches independent investigation into CEO after reports of suspected Chinese spy link.

Nvidia CEO warns US of dangers surrounding Chinese chip war.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”.

Despite his return, Nvidia confirmed that its independent investigation remains ongoing and that Huang has committed to cooperating with it.

The tech giant has also established a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. Nvidia is additionally searching for a Chief Compliance Officer and will continue cooperating with government investigations.

Industry News: AI-powered robot learns how to harvest tomatoes more efficiently

📅 18 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (462 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that farm labor shortages are pushing agriculture toward greater automation, especially when it comes to harvesting.
  • To tackle this challenge, Assistant Professor Takuya Fujinaga of Osaka Metropolitan University's Graduate School of Engineering developed a system that trains robots to assess how easy each tomato is to harvest before attempting to pick it.
  • In a recent development, his approach combines image recognition with statistical analysis to determine the best angle for picking each fruit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that farm labor shortages are pushing agriculture toward greater automation, especially when it comes to harvesting. But not all crops are easy for machines to handle. Tomatoes, for example, grow in clusters, which means a robot must carefully select ripe fruit while leaving unripe ones untouched. This requires precise control and smart decision-making.

To tackle this challenge, Assistant Professor Takuya Fujinaga of Osaka Metropolitan University's Graduate School of Engineering developed a system that trains robots to assess how easy each tomato is to harvest before attempting to pick it.

In a recent development, his approach combines image recognition with statistical analysis to determine the best angle for picking each fruit. The robot analyzes visual details such as the tomato itself, its stems, and whether it is hidden behind leaves or other parts of the plant. These inputs guide the robot in choosing the most effective way to approach and pick the fruit.

From Detection to "Harvest-Ease" Decision-Making.

This method shifts away from traditional systems that focus only on detecting and identifying fruit. Instead, Fujinaga introduces what he calls "harvest-ease estimation." "This moves beyond simply asking 'can a robot pick a tomato?' to thinking about 'how likely is a successful pick?', which is more meaningful for real-world farming," he explained.

In testing, the system achieved an 81% success rate, exceeding expectations. About one-quarter of the successful picks came from tomatoes that were harvested from the side after an initial front-facing attempt failed. This indicates the robot can adjust its approach when the first attempt is not successful.

According to recent reports, the research underscores how many variables affect robotic harvesting, including how tomatoes cluster, the shape and position of stems, surrounding leaves, and visual obstruction. "This research establishes 'ease of harvesting' as a quantitatively evaluable metric, bringing us one step closer to the realization of agricultural robots that can make informed decisions and act intelligently," Fujinaga mentioned.

Future of Human-Robot Collaboration in Farming.

Industry observers note that looking ahead, Fujinaga envisions robots that can independently judge when crops are ready to be picked. "This is expected to usher in a upcoming form of agriculture where robots and humans collaborate," he explained. "Robots will automatically harvest tomatoes that are easy to pick, while humans will handle the more challenging fruits.".

The findings were published in Smart Agricultural Technology.

Materials provided by Osaka Metropolitan University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Tech Report: DNA robots could deliver drugs and hunt viruses inside your body

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine tiny robots made from DNA moving through the bloodstream, delivering drugs exactly where they are needed and targeting threats such as cancer cells or viruses.
  • Industry observers note that researchers are exploring how DNA can be engineered into working machines using creative design approaches.
  • Industry observers note that guiding the motion of DNA robots in a constantly shifting molecular environment is a major challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine tiny robots made from DNA moving through the bloodstream, delivering drugs exactly where they are needed and targeting threats such as cancer cells or viruses. These microscopic machines could also assemble ultra-precise data storage systems and computing devices at the nanometer scale. Although the possibilities are remarkable, most DNA robots today remain in early experimental stages and are better understood as proof of concept rather than practical tools.

Industry observers note that researchers are exploring how DNA can be engineered into working machines using creative design approaches. These include building rigid DNA joints, incorporating flexible components, and using folding techniques inspired by origami. By applying principles from larger-scale robotics such as rigid, compliant and origami robots, scientists are adapting familiar mechanical concepts to the nanoscale. This allows DNA-based systems to carry out controlled and repeatable tasks despite their extremely small size.

Controlling Movement in DNA Nanorobots.

Industry observers note that guiding the motion of DNA robots in a constantly shifting molecular environment is a major challenge. To address this, scientists have developed control systems that help these machines behave in predictable ways. One important method involves DNA strand displacement, a biochemical process that enables precise programming of movement using specific DNA sequences labeled as "fuel" and "structure.".

It has been revealed that in addition to biochemical control, external physical signals such as electric fields, magnetic fields, and light can direct how these robots move. Together, these approaches provide a toolkit for fine-tuning the behavior of DNA machines with a high degree of accuracy.

DNA Robots in Medicine and Technology.

The potential uses for DNA robots extend well beyond laboratory experiments. In medicine, they could function as "nano-surgeons," locating diseased cells and delivering targeted treatments with precision. Researchers are also exploring whether these machines could capture viruses like SARS-CoV-2, with future systems potentially operating as fully autonomous drug delivery platforms.

DNA robots may also play a role in advanced manufacturing. Acting as programmable templates, they could position nanoparticles with sub-nanometer accuracy. This capability could lead to breakthroughs in molecular computing and highly efficient optical devices that outperform current technologies.

Challenges in Scaling DNA Robotics.

Despite rapid progress, several obstacles remain. Moving from large-scale systems to molecular machines introduces challenges such as Brownian motion, which makes precise control more difficult. Many current DNA robot designs are still relatively simple and operate in isolation, limiting their usefulness in complex real-world environments.

There are also gaps in foundational knowledge. Researchers still lack detailed databases describing the mechanical properties of DNA structures, and simulation tools for predicting behavior at this scale are not yet fully developed.

To overcome these barriers, scientists emphasize the need for collaboration across disciplines. Proposed solutions include creating standardized DNA "parts libraries," using artificial intelligence to improve design and simulation, and advancing bio-manufacturing methods. Progress in these areas will be essential for scaling DNA robots and integrating them into practical applications in healthcare, manufacturing, and beyond.

"The robots of tomorrow won't just be made of metal and plastic," states the research team. "They will be biological, programmable, and intelligent. They will be the tools that allow us to finally master the molecular world.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyberpunk 2’s creative director has joked that the sequel is “cancelled” after seeing what Rockstar has achieved with GTA 6.

GTA 6 has been making quite a splash since its long-awaited release on November 19, with Rockstar’s open-world game becoming the joint best-reviewed game of all time.

It’s so popular that teachers have had to send round a minibus to pick up absent students, while retirement home residents as old as 86 have also been playing.

The hype for GTA 6 has been so enormous that Rockstar reported $3.79 billion in estimated retail sales by the end of its first day, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history.

As you can imagine, this makes GTA 6 a particularly daunting game for other developers looking to follow in its footsteps. This is especially true for Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who joked that it has given him “GTAVI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression.”.

In a November 21 Bluesky post, Sarzynski praised GTA 6’s scale and attention to detail before joking that he was ready to give up game development and rake leaves instead.

According to recent reports, “GTAVI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now,” Sarzynski joked.

Despite the daunting task of following up GTA 6 with his own open-world game, Sarzynski remains positive that Cyberpunk 2 will offer fans something different.

Industry observers note that “Seriously though, I think we’re doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed,” he remarked.

Cyberpunk 2 currently doesn’t have a release date, but we do know that it’s being made with Unreal Engine 5 and entered pre-production in May 2025.

AI breakthrough cuts energy use by 100x while boosting accuracy

📅 06 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (913 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States.
  • Recent findings suggest that this rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability.
  • The research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States. According to the International Energy Agency, AI systems and data centers used about 415 terawatt hours of power in 2024. That accounts for more than 10% of the country's total electricity production, and demand is projected to double by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that this rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability. In response, researchers at a School of Engineering have created a proof-of-concept AI system designed to be far more efficient. Their approach could reduce energy use by up to 100 times while also improving performance on tasks.

A Hybrid Approach Called Neuro-Symbolic AI.

The research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor. His team is developing neuro-symbolic AI, which combines traditional neural networks with symbolic reasoning. This method mirrors how people approach problems by breaking them into steps and categories.

The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation in Vienna in May and will appear in the conference proceedings.

Teaching Robots to See, Understand, and Act.

Recent findings suggest that unlike familiar large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini, the team focuses on AI systems used in robotics. These systems are known as visual-language-action (VLA) models. They extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement.

VLA models take in visual data from cameras and instructions from language, then translate that information into real-world actions. For example, they can control a robot's wheels, arms, or fingers to complete a task.

Why Traditional AI Struggles With Simple Tasks.

In a recent development, conventional VLA systems rely heavily on data and trial-and-error learning. If a robot is asked to stack blocks into a tower, it must first analyze the scene, identify each block, and determine how to place them correctly.

This process often leads to mistakes. Shadows may confuse the system about a block's shape, or the robot may place pieces incorrectly, causing the structure to collapse.

These errors are similar to the problems seen in LLMs. Just as robots can misplace blocks, chatbots can generate false or misleading outputs. Examples include fabricating legal cases or producing images with unrealistic details such as extra fingers.

How Symbolic Reasoning Improves Accuracy and Efficiency.

Industry observers note that symbolic reasoning offers a different strategy. Instead of relying only on patterns from data, it uses rules and abstract concepts such as shape and balance. This allows the system to plan more effectively and avoid unnecessary trial and error.

"Like an LLM, VLA models act on statistical results from large training sets of similar scenarios, but that can lead to errors," noted Scheutz. "A neuro-symbolic VLA can apply rules that limit the amount of trial and error during learning and get to a solution much faster. Not only does it complete the task much faster, but the time spent on training the system is significantly reduced.".

The researchers tested their system using the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, a classic problem that requires careful planning.

In a recent development, the neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate, compared with just 34% for standard systems. When given a more complex version of the puzzle that it had not encountered before, the hybrid system still succeeded 78% of the time. Traditional models failed every attempt.

In a recent development, training time also dropped sharply. The new system learned the task in only 34 minutes, while conventional models required more than a day and a half.

Massive Energy Savings in Training and Use.

It has been revealed that energy consumption was reduced dramatically as well. Training the neuro-symbolic model required only 1% of the energy used by a standard VLA system. During operation, it used just 5% of the energy needed by conventional approaches.

Scheutz compared this inefficiency to everyday AI tools. "These systems are just trying to predict the next word or action in a sequence, but that can be imperfect, and they can come up with inaccurate results or hallucinations. Their energy expense is often disproportionate to the task. For example, when you search on Google, the AI summary at the top of the page consumes up to 100 times more energy than the generation of the website listings.".

The Growing Strain of AI on Power Infrastructure.

Sources indicate that as AI adoption accelerates across industries, demand for computing power continues to climb. Companies are building increasingly large data centers, some of which require hundreds of megawatts of electricity. That level of consumption can exceed the needs of entire small cities.

This trend has sparked a race to expand infrastructure, raising concerns about long-term energy limits.

The researchers suggest that current approaches based on LLMs and VLAs may not be sustainable in the long run. While these systems are powerful, they consume large amounts of energy and can still produce unreliable results.

In contrast, neuro-symbolic AI offers a different direction. By combining learning with structured reasoning, it may provide a more efficient and dependable foundation for future AI systems.

Materials provided by Tufts University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

This new chip survives 1300°F (700°C) and could change AI forever

📅 07 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that modern electronics power everything from smartphones to satellites, but they all share a major limitation.
  • Researchers at the University of Southern California now believe they have found a way past that limit.
  • In a study published on March 26, 2026 in Science, a team led by Joshua Yang, Arthur B.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that modern electronics power everything from smartphones to satellites, but they all share a major limitation. Heat. Once temperatures climb above roughly 200 degrees Celsius, most devices begin to break down. For decades, this thermal barrier has been one of the toughest challenges in engineering.

Researchers at the University of Southern California now believe they have found a way past that limit.

In a study published on March 26, 2026 in Science, a team led by Joshua Yang, Arthur B. Freeman Chair Professor at the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering and the USC School of Advanced Computing, unveiled a new type of memory device that continues to operate at 700 degrees Celsius (~1300 degrees Fahrenheit). That temperature exceeds molten lava and goes far beyond anything previously achieved for this class of technology. The device showed no sign of failure. In fact, 700 degrees was simply the maximum their equipment could test.

"You may call it a revolution," Yang said. "It is the best high-temperature memory ever demonstrated.".

A Memristor Built for Extreme Heat.

In a recent development, the fresh device is known as a memristor, a nanoscale component that can both store data and perform computations. It is constructed like a microscopic layered structure, with two electrodes on either side and a thin ceramic layer in between.

Industry observers note that jian Zhao, the study's first author, built the device using tungsten for the top electrode, hafnium oxide ceramic in the middle, and graphene for the bottom layer. Tungsten has the highest melting point of any element, while graphene, a single-atom-thick sheet of carbon, is known for its exceptional strength and heat resistance.

According to recent reports, this combination produced remarkable performance. The device retained data for more than 50 hours at 700 degrees without needing to be refreshed. It also endured over one billion switching cycles at that temperature and operated at just 1.5 volts with speeds measured in tens of nanoseconds.

The discovery was not part of the team's original plan. They were initially attempting to create a different graphene-based device, which did not work as intended. Along the way, they encountered something surprising.

"To be honest, it was by accident, as most discoveries are," Yang said. "If you can predict it, it's usually not surprising, and probably not significant enough.".

In a recent development, further investigation revealed why the device performed so well. In conventional electronics, heat causes metal atoms in the top electrode to slowly migrate through the ceramic layer. Eventually, they reach the bottom electrode, creating a permanent connection that short-circuits the device and leaves it stuck in the on state.

Graphene prevents this failure. Its interaction with tungsten is, as Yang described it, similar to oil and water. Tungsten atoms that approach the graphene surface cannot attach to it. Without a stable point to settle, they drift away instead of forming a conductive bridge. This prevents short circuits and preserves the device's function even under extreme heat.

The researchers confirmed this mechanism using advanced electron microscopy, spectroscopy, and quantum-level simulations. By understanding what happens at the atomic interface, they have turned an unexpected result into a principle that could guide future designs. Other materials with similar surface properties could be identified, which may help scale the technology for industrial production.

Applications in Extreme Environments.

Electronics capable of operating above 500 degrees Celsius have long been a goal for space exploration. Venus, for example, has a surface temperature around that level, and every lander sent there has failed in part due to extreme heat. Current silicon-based chips cannot survive such conditions.

"We are now above 700 degrees, and we suspect it will go higher," Yang stated.

The potential applications go far beyond space missions. Geothermal energy systems require electronics that can function deep underground, where surrounding rock can glow red-hot. Nuclear and fusion systems also expose equipment to intense heat. Even in everyday settings, durability improves significantly. A device rated for 700 degrees would be extremely robust at the roughly 125-degree temperatures often reached inside automotive electronics.

Why It Matters for Artificial Intelligence.

In addition to storing data, the device offers a major advantage for artificial intelligence. Many AI systems rely heavily on matrix multiplication, a mathematical operation used in tasks like image recognition and language processing. Traditional computers perform these calculations step by step, consuming large amounts of energy.

According to recent reports, memristors approach the problem differently. By using Ohm's Law, where voltage times conductance equals current, the device performs calculations directly as electricity flows through it. The result is obtained instantly as the measured current.

"Over 92 percent of the computing in AI systems like ChatGPT is nothing but matrix multiplication," Yang noted. "This type of device can perform that in the most efficient way, orders of magnitude faster and at lower energy.".

Yang and three co-authors of the study (Qiangfei Xia, Miao Hu, and Ning Ge) have already co-founded a manufacturer called TetraMem to commercialize memristor-based AI chips at room temperature. Their lab is already using working chips from TetraMem for machine learning tasks. The high-temperature version described in this research could extend those capabilities to environments where traditional electronics cannot operate, allowing devices such as spacecraft or industrial sensors to process data directly on site.

From Lab Prototype to Real-World Technology.

According to recent reports, despite the promising results, Yang emphasizes that practical applications are still some distance away. Memory is only one part of a complete computing system. High-temperature logic circuits will also need to be developed and integrated. In addition, the current devices were built manually at very small scales in a laboratory setting, so manufacturing at scale will take time.

"This is the first step," Yang mentioned. "It's still a long way to go. But logically, you can see: now it makes it possible. The missing component has been made.".

Sources indicate that from a manufacturing perspective, two of the materials used in the device, tungsten and hafnium oxide, are already widely used in semiconductor production. Graphene is newer but is actively being developed by major companies such as TSMC and Samsung, and it has already been produced at wafer scale in research environments.

Industry observers note that the work was conducted through the CONCRETE Center, short for Center of Neuromorphic Computing under Extreme Environments, a multi-university Center of Excellence led by USC and supported by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research and the Air Force Research Laboratory. Key experimental work was carried out in collaboration with Dr. Sabyasachi Ganguli's team at the AFRL Materials Lab in Dayton, Ohio, while theoretical analysis involved USC researchers and collaborators at Kumamoto University in Japan.

For Yang, publication in Science reflects more than a single achievement.

In a recent development, "Space exploration has never been so real, so close, and at such a large scale," he said. "This paper represents a critical leap into a much larger, more exciting frontier.".

Materials provided by University of Southern California. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

GTA 6 hacker released from prison after judge warns him not to do it again

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The hacker responsible for the massive GTA 6 leak in 2022 has been released from prison after receiving a seven-year sentence, with a judge warning him not to return to cybercrime.
  • Arion Kurtaj, 21, was sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court on November 23, but walked free the same day after already serving the majority of his sentence in custody.
  • According to the BBC, the former Lapsus$ hacker has been released on license and given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including banning him from using Telegram and Discord.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The hacker responsible for the massive GTA 6 leak in 2022 has been released from prison after receiving a seven-year sentence, with a judge warning him not to return to cybercrime.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, was sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court on November 23, but walked free the same day after already serving the majority of his sentence in custody.

According to the BBC, the former Lapsus$ hacker has been released on license and given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including banning him from using Telegram and Discord.

“You are a very talented young man,” Mr Justice Turner told Kurtaj before warning him: “Don’t let this happen again.”.

Kurtaj made headlines in September 2022 when he hacked Rockstar Games and leaked 90 clips containing nearly an hour of GTA 6 gameplay, revealing Vice City and the game’s two protagonists long before its official announcement.

Remarkably, the teenager carried out the attack while on bail for other cybercrimes, using an Amazon Fire Stick, a television, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse from a Travelodge hotel.

He also attempted to blackmail Rockstar, threatening to release the game’s source code unless the developer contacted him.

Rockstar later revealed that the breach cost the company approximately $5 million to recover from, alongside thousands of hours of staff time.

In December 2023, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital after being deemed unfit to stand trial due to his autism.

At the time, the court heard that he remained highly motivated to commit further cybercrimes and could potentially hack Rockstar again.

However, a subsequent assessment found him fit to stand trial, and he was moved to a conventional prison in January 2026.

Recent findings suggest that even while behind bars, Kurtaj made headlines again in March after allegedly using a smuggled phone to post about GTA 6. He later pleaded guilty to possessing a mobile phone in prison.

On November 16, Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar hack and several other cybercrimes involving companies including Uber, Revolut, and BT/EE.

His release comes just days after GTA 6 officially launched on November 19, more than four years after his original attack.

Meanwhile, Rockstar has faced another wave of GTA 6 leaks from the anonymous Cyberleek in 2026, including gameplay footage and claims of access to development builds.
